position: Clear and Restrictive Rules on Guidance Documents
proposal: The Mandate recommends that DOL reinstitute, through notice and comment, its 2020 PRO Good Guidance rule, which limited the use of guidance in enforcement, barred treating guidance as binding, required guidance to be posted in a searchable database, and let the public comment on creating, revising and rescinding guidance. It also asks Congress to amend the Administrative Procedure Act to limit the use of guidance documents.
remaining: A notice-and-comment rule limiting DOL's use of guidance
Congressional amendment of the Administrative Procedure Act

status_summary: No Federal Register document reinstating the DOL good guidance rule was found for the period since 2025-01-20. DOL announced an expanded opinion letter program on 2025-06-02, and on 2025-07-02 proposed to remove FLSA interpretive rules from the CFR and recast them as sub-regulatory guidance; neither restores the 2020 rule. The Wage and Hour Division withdrew that 2025-07-02 proposal in a notice published 2026-10-07, without mentioning the 2020 rule or new guidance procedures.

timeline.event: DOL announced an expanded opinion letter program covering five of its agencies.
DOL published a proposed rule to remove FLSA interpretive rules and policy statements from Title 29 of the CFR and repurpose them as sub-regulatory guidance.

DOL Wage and Hour Division published the withdrawal (effective 2026-10-06) of its 2025-07-02 proposed rule to remove interpretive rules not issued through notice and comment from Title 29 and recast them as sub-regulatory guidance, ending that rulemaking.

title: Reinstate DOL's good guidance rule through notice and comment
uncertainties: No Federal Register document reinstating the DOL good guidance rule was found. The Labor Unified Agenda rule list on reginfo.gov (Agency Rule List - 2026) lists only the Wage and Hour interpretive statements item (RIN 1235-AA52), which the division withdrew in a notice published 2026-10-07 and which the agenda still shows with a final rule projected for August 2026; it is not the recommended action. S. 252 would require online posting of guidance government-wide; its reported substitute text was not read. A DOL internal guidance policy would not appear in the Federal Register, and the opinion letter expansion rests on a law firm description. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
